messages:
maria_support: FYI — support ticket from Acme.ai: after they enabled KV cache + continuous batching they see periodic 429 + big tail latency during short bursts (30 requests in ~5s). customer says quotas look fine. attaching minimal repro.

sam_engineer: can you paste the repro steps & any header/errors they get? 429 body? sampling of logs?

julia_csm: customer is hitting this in prod, high priority for them. they see token-level 429s and some 502s after retries.

maria_support: Repro steps from customer (copied):
```
# warmup cache
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"id_'$i' prefix-sample"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null &
done
# then burst
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"user request '$i'"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
Responses: ~6 of the 30 return `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` with body `{ "error": "rate_limited", "retry_after": 1 }`, and ~4 responses are 500/502. Latency median rises from ~90ms to ~700ms during burst tail.

sam_engineer: thanks. quick checklist:
- are they using a shared API key or org-level quota?
- check X-RateLimit-* headers on 200 responses (Remaining, Reset)
- what's the per-customer burst window / refill rate configured on infra?
- KV cache hit rate during burst?

jon_eng_runtime: adding runtime notes: we recently changed continuous batching flush_win -> 8ms for some customers; that can increase per-request queuing during tight bursts if batch shaping + KV cache misses coincide. Two common patterns I've seen:
1) KV cache prefix cardinality too high (cache miss for many unique prefixes) -> more compute per request -> slower per-token throughput -> router starts shedding under token-bucket limits -> 429s.
2) Batch sizing oscillation: initial fast requests create small batches which underutilize GPU, downstream requests queue and form larger batches but exceed per-customer burst allowance before token-bucket refills.

jon_eng_runtime: what to check right now:
- router.q_len and serving.batch.size histograms during the window
- runtime.metrics.kv_cache.hit_rate (per-prefix)
- per-api-key token_bucket.credits and refill_rate
- gpu_util and kernel_latency spikes

sam_engineer: recommended immediate mitigations to try for the customer:
- temporarily reduce continuous batching max_wait_ms to 2-4ms (less batching jitter).
- disable KV prefetch or reduce prefetch window (if they used prefetch heavily) to avoid overload of KV subsystem.
- increase token bucket burst_size for that API key (if org policy allows).
- add exponential backoff+jitter on client for bursts.

maria_support: customer says they have large org quota and burst_size was set high, so not obvious quota exhaustion. they did enable a prefix-based cache: user_id:session_id:prompt_hash -> many unique session ids.

jon_eng_runtime: that prefix pattern is likely the root: many unique prefixes -> very low hit rate -> KV cache not helping but adds overhead (prefetch/lookup) which increases latency per request versus straight pass-through. When batching tries to coalesce requests, some are slower due to KV lookups so batch completion time increases and token bucket depletes.

sam_engineer: can you ask them to run a small telemetry command to dump headers & a kv hit sample? Example curl to capture headers:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Look for: `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, `X-Redwood-KV-Hit: true/false`, and `X-Request-ID`.

maria_support: sent that to them. they replied with a sample: most 200s show `X-Redwood-KV-Hit: false`, Remaining ~580, Reset in ~60s. 429s show Remaining: 0, Reset: 1.

julia_csm: customer reaction: they were assuming KV cache would reduce load but because of session-based prefixes it didn't. They want recommendation to avoid 429s in short term.

jon_eng_runtime: short term: change cache key to a lower-cardinality prefix (e.g., user_id:prompt_type) so hits increase. Also set continuous batching wait lower and enable a per-key queue limit so a few slow lookups don't block others (we can route to a fast-path without KV).

sam_engineer: I'll open an internal runtime ticket to add a short-circuit fast-path option: if KV hit rate < 10% for 1m we skip prefetch for that key. For now, we can add a transient per-org burst increase too.

maria_support: customer accepted workaround: they'll change keying and throttle client burst with small token-bucket + 100ms jitter backoff.

deploy-bot: runtime: rolling deploy to canary with `batch_max_wait_ms=3` for group:acme-ai (canary) — started.

jon_eng_runtime: once canary is healthy let's monitor `serving.batch.latency_p95`, `router.drop.rate`, and `runtime.kv.hitrate`. I will also correlate `token_bucket.credits` for the key during the next customer test.

maria_support: thanks all. will update ticket. :thumbsup:

sam_engineer: follow-ups: add quick doc snippet for customers about "KV cache key design" and "burst-proofing clients". low-effort FAQ would cut a lot of these.

julia_csm: posting suggested FAQ to #docs after this thread.

maria_support: closing loop here once customer confirms improved behavior — keeping thread open until then.
